knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The lesson says to count only billable hours, since visits, travel, admin, marketing, training and leave are not billable. Building the rate from billable hours lets the work that is billed cover the costs and income.
The lesson says a short visit still pays for travel, set-up and admin, so a minimum charge covers that time. The other options contradict the lesson.
The lesson says to start from your own costs and billable hours and then compare with local evidence. A single vendor's average, a friend's rate or a platform's listing is not the recommended check.

practicalCriteria: Learner calculates billable hours from a one-month log, showing each non-billable deduction.
Learner builds a base rate from a worksheet of annual costs and an income target, showing the calculation.
Learner sets a minimum charge for a short job and writes the wording the client will see before the visit.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
stopWorkCriteria: Stop work if procedure step 1 is not done: Estimate paid hours in a year, then subtract visit travel, admin, marketing, training and leave to find billable hours.
